segments.title: What each call prints once its bug is fixed

steps.caption: isYes gets a YES made with new, so an object of its own. The literal YES it is checked against is a different object, in the pool.
Bug 1 compared the arrows, which lead to two different objects, so it said false. Comparing the characters instead says true.
hasKeyword gets null for its text: no object at all, so there is nothing to search. Bug 2 called a method through null and crashed. Checking for null first answers false.
firstThree gets Strings, indexes 0 to 6. A substring leaves its end index out, so ending at 3 takes S, t and r. Bug 3 ended at 4 and took one too many.
removeDots gets 1.2.3. Bug 4 used a pattern, in which a dot means any character, so every character went. Removing plain dots keeps 123.
shout gets hi. Upper-casing builds a new String, HI, and bug 5 threw it away, returning hi. Returning the new String gives HI.
Fix the five labelled bugs in BuggyStrings. Then write the calls in main, run it with ▶, then press Check my output.

segments.title: What if the end index is past the end?

steps.caption: Strings has 7 characters, indexes 0 to 6. An end index can be at most 7, the length.
An end index of 8 would need a character at index 7, which does not exist: the program crashes.
steps.error: StringIndexOutOfBoundsException: Range [0, 8) out of bounds for length 7

steps.caption: shout gets hi. Upper-casing builds a new String, HI, and hands back an arrow to it, but nothing catches that arrow.
So text still points at hi, and that is what comes back. Before calling a String method, ask: it returns a new String, am I catching it?
